sources.entry: dash - A framework for building data apps and dashboards in pure Python, built on Plotly.

summary.one_liner: Dash is a Python framework for building interactive data science and ML web apps and dashboards, built on Plotly.js, React and Flask.
summary.what_it_does: Dash lets you tie UI elements such as dropdowns, sliders and graphs directly to Python analytical code, so apps update reactively when a user changes an input. The README says apps are written in pure Python, and that the framework uses Plotly.js for charting with about 50 chart types, including maps. It also says Dash is not limited to dashboards, since layout and styling can be customized, with an example app styled to look like a PDF report. Example apps mentioned include one that pulls data from Google Finance into a Pandas DataFrame and one with five inputs, three outputs and cross filtering. The README points to docs, a user guide and a dash.gallery of example apps with Python and R code. Dash Open Source runs apps locally; the README says Dash Enterprise is a separate commercial offering for hosting, deployment, authentication and related features.
use_cases: build interactive data dashboards in Python
turn analysis code into a web app
create ML and data science web apps
add dropdowns and sliders to plotly charts
prototype a data tool to run on a laptop
notable: Reactive callbacks connect Python functions to UI inputs and outputs
About 50 Plotly.js chart types, including maps
Apps are written entirely in Python, with no required CSS for basic styling
Public app gallery at dash.gallery with Python and R code
Commercial Dash Enterprise adds hosting, auth and job queue on top of the open-source framework
caveats: Dash Open Source apps run locally and are not easily shared with others in an organization, per the README
Scaling, hosting, authentication and job queues are part of the paid Dash Enterprise offering
